h: The Three Mouths Prepare for the Word of Hashem

p: In the holy Zohar on this parashah (201b):
"The mouth of Hashem" is the middah of Malchus,
which is the aspect of the day of Shabbos,
And in the holy Zohar (Zohar I 32a):
"By the word of Hashem the heavens were made";
that is, in all the utterances of the works of Creation
אַךְ אַחַר כָּךְ אַחַר כָּל הַבְּרִיאָה
but afterward, after all of Creation,
"on the day that Hashem Elokim made
the attribute of mercy to the attribute of judgment,
the aspect of "the mouth of Hashem."
And this is "by the word of"
which is the aspect of mercy
and the mouth in the soul.
דְּאֵין הַפֵּירוּשׁ שֶׁאָז נִבְרָא הַפֶּה בְּנֶפֶשׁ
that the meaning is not that the mouth in the soul was created then;
when he was created on Erev Shabbos,
נִבְרָא גַּם כֵּן עִם כֹּחַ הַדִּיבּוּר
was also created with the power of speech,
that on Shabbos, when "the mouth of Hashem ascends,"
then the mouth in the soul was made;
that is, that a person have it in his power
that be the word of Hashem, the mouth of Hashem;
and that is the aspect of the Oral Torah:
דְּבָרַי אֲשֶׁר שַׂמְתִּי בְּפִיךָ (יְשַׁעְיָה נט, כא)
"My words that I have put in your mouth" (Yeshayahu 59:21);
"The word of Hashem — this is halachah."
כָּל מָקוֹם אֲשֶׁר אַזְכִּיר אֶת שְׁמִי
"In every place where I will mention My Name";
and "the Name of Hashem" is Torah,
regarding the blessing over the Torah before it,
"When I call the Name of Hashem,
And so they learned from this (Berachos 6a)
that one who sits and toils in Torah
But in the Torah that one learns,
it is in truth "the mouth of Hashem,"
and this is "I will mention My Name";
and this is with the voice of Torah.
And likewise with the voice of prayer:
in the name of our master, the Rebbe Reb Elimelech,
"From where do we know that HaKadosh Baruch Hu prays?"
that is, through the mouths of Yisrael;
and this is "If my prayer is fluent in my mouth,"
an expression of being sent from Hashem Yisbarach;
and this is the aspect of "the mouth of Hashem"
and this is the meaning of the creation of the mouth in the soul.
אַךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמַר בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ מִקּוֹדֶם
But what the holy Zohar said before,
that on Erev Shabbos at twilight
there were created the mouth of the well,
of the earth, and the mouth of the donkey,
"the day became holy," as mentioned above
אֵיזֶה שַׁיָּיכוּת יֵשׁ לָהֶם לְפִי ה׳
what connection they have to "the mouth of Hashem,"
that they were a preparation for it.
But the mouth of the well
the well was in the merit of Miriam;
and Miriam is the aspect of the moon,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג קפא, ב)
is the middah of Malchus, the mouth,
And so it is expounded in the Gemara (Eruvin 54a):
the Torah is given to him as a gift;
and this is for the reason
that the well alludes to words of Torah;
is given to him as a gift,
so that it is called "his Torah,"
and then "in his Torah he meditates."
וְלָזֶה הָיָה זֶה הַפִּי בְּאֵר הֲכָנָה
And for this, this mouth of the well was a preparation
that there also be in the soul
the aspect of "the mouth of Hashem":
"My words that I have put in your mouth."
And likewise the mouth of the earth
הַיְינוּ נֶגֶד מִי שֶׁכּוֹפֵר בְּפִי ה׳
is against one who denies "the mouth of Hashem,"
who disputed with Moshe and Aharon;
for this the mouth of the earth was created,
so that he would have a repair
"The wicked, even at the entrance of Gehinnom,
this refers to the sinners of Yisrael, etc."
That is, the sinners of Yisrael
"Moshe is true and his Torah is true,
which is the mouth of the earth;
וְהַיְינוּ עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (עֵירוּבִין שָׁם)
and that is according to what it says (Eruvin 19a):
וַיֵּרְדוּ הֵם וְכָל אֲשֶׁר לָהֶם וְגוֹ׳
"And they and all that was theirs went down, etc."
שֶׁגַּם שָׁם יְכוֹלִים לְהַכִּיר פִּי ה׳
for there too one can recognize "the mouth of Hashem."
correspond to what it says in the Midrash

p: But the mouth of the donkey
what connection and preparation was this
'And Hashem opened the mouth of the donkey,'
it is brought in the Gemara (Bava Basra 14b):
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינָן צוֹרְכֵי מֹשֶׁה וְתוֹרָתוֹ וְכוּלֵּי
"even though they are not the concern of Moshe and his Torah, etc."
וְקָשֶׁה לָמָּה נָקַט דַּוְקָא פָּרָשַׁת בִּלְעָם
And it is difficult: why did it single out the passage of Bilam
more than the other narratives in the Torah,
such as all of Sefer Bereishis?
And if because of the need of Yisrael
the passage of Bilam too is for the need of Yisrael;
"These are the kings who reigned, etc.,"
and as the holy Zohar lists
such as the words of Esav,
Also, why is it called the passage of Bilam
and not the passage of Balak,
וְכֵן הוּזְכְּרָה בְּלָשׁוֹן זֶה בַּגְּמָרָא (בְּרָכוֹת יב, ב)
And so it is mentioned in this wording in the Gemara (Berachos 12b):
"They sought to establish the passage of Balak
Also in the holy Zohar there:
"the words of Balak, the words of Bilam."
in the name of the Ritva,
that there was a separate book
But this is difficult to say,
for all books apart from Tanach
were not permitted to be written,
and they are called external books.
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בְּסִפְרֵי (פָּרָשַׁת בְּרָכָה)
according to what is written in Sifrei (Parashas Berachah):
וְלֹא קָם נָבִיא עוֹד בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל כְּמֹשֶׁה
"'And there has not arisen again a prophet in Yisrael like Moshe' (Devarim 34:10)
but among the nations of the world there arose;
and who is this? Bilam, etc."
וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (סִפְרֵי מַטּוֹת)
And this follows what is written (Sifrei, Matos):
that the prophets prophesied with "Thus said";
for he prophesied with "This is the thing."
That is, the prophets prophesied with "Thus said,"
for first they heard the prophecy
while Moshe prophesied with "This is the thing":
that is, at the moment he said the prophecy,
then the Shechinah spoke from within his throat;
and that is "This is the thing,"
as if pointing with a finger.
And in the holy Zohar (this parashah, 210b):
she will speak the words, etc."
That is, he was not the one speaking;
only the Shechinah was the one speaking.
that I speak to you, that shall you do"
what is the expression "shall you do"?
It should have said "shall you speak."
And earlier, "to do anything small or great"
but here, where it is only speech,
what is the expression "shall you do"?
But it is according to what was said:
and he would only make the movements
of the articulation of the mouth;
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ שֶׁאָמַר (בָּבָא מְצִיעָא צ, ב)
along the lines of what it says (Bava Metzia 90b):
"The twisting of his mouth is considered an act."
וְאַחַר כָּךְ בְּמַאֲמַר הַמַּלְאָךְ לְבִלְעָם (שָׁם כב, לה)
And afterward, in the angel's statement to Bilam (Bamidbar 22:35),
"what I speak to you, that shall you speak,"
that God will put in his mouth,
And Bilam, to Balak, the first time
And afterward, when he saw further
that it was not in his power through his speech,
"that shall I take care to speak":
that is, he is only like a guard
עַל הַדְּבָרִים אֲשֶׁר יָשִׂים ה׳ בְּפִיו
over the words that Hashem will put in his mouth.
And afterward, as it is written (Bamidbar 23:16),
"And He put a word in his mouth"
and it is brought (in the Midrash Rabbah):
הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא פּוֹקֵס אֶת פִּיו וְכוּלֵּי
HaKadosh Baruch Hu bridled his mouth, etc.
that it was not in his power even to be silent,
כֹּל אֲשֶׁר יְדַבֵּר ה׳ אוֹתוֹ אֶעֱשֶׂה
"All that Hashem speaks, that shall I do":
that is, he is only the doer,
through the twisting of his mouth,
And afterward, as it is written (Bamidbar 24:2),
"And the spirit of God was upon him,"
"The words of one who hears the sayings of God, etc.";
"What Hashem speaks, that shall I speak"
שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ גַּם כֵּן חֵלֶק בְּהַדִּיבּוּר
that he too had a share in the speech.
עַל יְדֵי שֶׁנִּכְתְּבוּ עַל יְדֵי מֹשֶׁה
the words of Esav, the words of Lavan;
עַל זֶה אָמַר מֹשֶׁה כָּתַב סִפְרוֹ
about this it says "Moshe wrote his book,"
for they are all included in his book.
And likewise the words of Balak,
what he said and the events,
הוּא גַּם כֵּן בִּכְלַל כָּתַב סִפְרוֹ
are also included in "wrote his book";
for through his writing them in the Torah
And although the Torah preceded the world
for it is called by his name;
וּמִשּׁוּם הָכִי לֹא הוּזְכַּר פָּרָשַׁת בָּלָק
And therefore the passage of Balak is not mentioned.
שֶׁבָּזֶה לֹא הָיָה צָרִיךְ לְחַדֵּשׁ דָּבָר
in which he did not need to innovate anything,
for in truth they were the word of Hashem,
and performed the act of the articulation of the mouth
since it is not included in "wrote his book."
This is not so there in the Gemara,
"they sought to establish the passage of Balak
until after the prophecy of Bilam;
for to establish the passage of Bilam,
that Moshe Rabbeinu did not divide,
there is no break of a section
until after the end of the prophecy of Bilam;
and it would have been necessary to establish
his words together with the events;
and therefore the Gemara called it the passage of Balak:
the words of Balak and the words of Bilam,
until the end of the passage.

p: of the mouth of the donkey being created
that is, that this power was then created,
that there could be the aspect of "the mouth of Hashem"
even when it comes out of the mouth of Bilam;
in the aspect of the donkey,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ רז, א)
as it says in the holy Zohar (this parashah, 207a).
And that is "the mouth of the donkey":
from the aspect of "the mouth of Hashem"
through the articulation of Bilam's mouth,
which is the mouth of the donkey.
And "the mouth of the donkey" indicates
does not sense at all what he is saying,
nevertheless one can learn from it.
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (יְשַׁעְיָה ל, כא)
And this is along the lines of what is said (Yeshayahu 30:21),
"And your ears shall hear a word behind you,
saying: This is the way, walk in it."
that is, even if he hears from a gentile
he should learn from it some conduct
in the service of Hashem Yisbarach;
for not for nothing were heard
And like the matter that is told
מֵהָרַבִּי רַבִּי זוּשָׁא זֵכֶר צַדִּיק לִבְרָכָה
of the Rebbe Reb Zusha, zecher tzaddik livrachah,
that once he was walking on the road,
and a gentile was driving a wagon of fodder,
and it overturned to the ground.
The Rebbe Reb Zusha answered him
the lower hei has fallen to the ground,
and it is within my ability to lift it,
but I do not want to!"
And in the Mishnah (beginning of chapter 4 of Avos)
One who learns from every person,
'From all my teachers I have gained understanding'";
and they did not bring the pasuk
"And your ears shall hear a word, etc.,"
as they brought it in the Gemara (Megillah 32a)
to learn that one may make use of a bas kol.
But from the wording of the Mishnah,
which says "Who is wise? One who learns,"
it is evident that it refers
to one who wishes to learn from him,
and he intends to teach him;
about this it says "from every person"
for so it is also in the language of the Sages:
as the Tosfos Yom Tov writes
אִם הָרַב דּוֹמֶה לְמַלְאַךְ ה׳ צְבָאוֹת
"If the teacher resembles an angel of Hashem of Hosts,
let them seek Torah from his mouth, etc.,"
learn Torah from the mouth of Acher?"
And they answered: "This refers to a great person, etc.";
One who learns from every person":
for a great person can learn;
and on this it brings the pasuk,
even though he does not resemble, etc.,
nevertheless I gained understanding from it.
where it is written, "shall hear a word behind you":
who speaks for his own purpose
and does not intend to teach you,
"saying: This is the way, walk in it";
and this is the matter of a bas kol.
And as we find (Yerushalmi, chapter 6 of Shabbos),
where they heard a bas kol from people
the intent of their own speech,
and they learned from it for their own matter;
and it also brings the pasuk,
And this is the meaning of "the mouth of the donkey":
that even in the mouth of the donkey
there can be the word of Hashem.
is in exile among the nations;
and the main thing is what it says (Pesachim 87b):
"only so that converts be added to them"
that is, in order to bring out
"And You give life to them all."
And the essence of life is in words of Torah;
that is, in all of them there are words of Torah
and Yisrael brings out from them
And this is "And your ears shall hear
that is, even from a gentile,
and even if he does not intend at all to teach you,
וְתָבִין אֶת זֶה הַדֶּרֶךְ לְכוּ בוֹ
and understand "this is the way, walk in it."
And this is "the mouth of the donkey":
that in the mouth of the donkey there can be
the aspect of the Oral Torah.
And this is why it was created before
and that is "Malchus is the mouth";
that on Shabbos the mouth in the soul was created,
that is, that "the mouth of Hashem" should speak.
